thread:
maureen (docs): Heads-up — I found inconsistent wording around our data-aging policy in the SOC2 audit-logs docs. Some places say 'retain for X days' and others say 'exportable for X days'. We should standardize to avoid audit confusion.

samir (security): Good catch. Can you paste the two spots? I can propose a short, SOC2-friendly line.

maureen (docs): Sure — snippet A from /audit-exports.md: `Logs are retained for 365 days and available for export.`
snippet B from /evidence/export-playbook.md: `Exportable for one year; retention may vary.`

maureen (docs): My proposal: "Audit logs are retained by Redwood for 365 days; customers may export their tenant logs within that retention window. For SOC 2 evidence, see export and export-retention details." Short and prescriptive. Thoughts?

lee (legal): I like clarity but avoid implying unilateral retention changes. Suggest: "Redwood retains audit logs for 365 days by default; customers are responsible for exporting or archiving logs needed for their audits within that retention period." That shifts operational responsibility correctly.

samir (security): Lee's edit reads safer. Also add a note about encryption & HSM: "Exports are delivered encrypted in transit; for long-term storage, customers should use their KMS/HSM as required by policy."

alex (sdk): Related — the Python SDK snippet in the export docs uses `client.export_logs(tenant_id, days=365)`. We deprecated `days` flag in v2. Need to update examples to use `export_window_days` and show the `format` arg. Example:```py
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
c.export_logs(tenant_id="t_123", export_window_days=365, format="jsonl")
```

maureen (docs): Thanks. I'll update the docs copy to Lee's wording + Samir's encryption sentence, and switch the code snippet to Alex's example.

ci-bot: build #4821 for docs/audit-exports.md started by @maureen.

alex (sdk): One more: add a short note about SDK migration for older clients: `Legacy: client.export_logs(tenant_id, days=...)` -> `v2: export_window_days` and include a one-line migration command for pip: `pip install redwood-sdk==2.*`

samir (security): Also add a quick cross-ref to incident response: when logs are requested for an investigation outside the retention window, include the legal/ops contact path. "Contact security@redwood.dev for retention exceptions."

maureen (docs): Will do. I'll make a PR with the three edits (copy, snippet, migration note) and ping legal + security for quick sign-off. PR description will include links to audit-policy and export CLI.

lee (legal): Please include the exact SOC2 phrasing: "for SOC 2 Type II evidence, customers should ensure exports are performed within the retention period to meet evidence requests."

maureen (docs): Got it — adding that sentence. Drafting now. ETA: PR in ~45m.

alex (sdk): If you want I can drop a small test snippet in the SDK repo to validate the example; will link it in the PR.

maureen (docs): That would be great — thanks. I'll tag you in the PR. :thumbsup:

samir (security): Thanks all. Small follow-up after PR: can we add a docs-console screenshot showing the export flow? auditors often ask for screenshots.

maureen (docs): Good idea — will capture one during the PR and add alt text.

ci-bot: build #4821 succeeded (6m 12s).

maureen (docs): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/721 — includes wording change, SDK snippet update, migration note, and screenshot. Please review.

lee (legal): Reviewing now.

samir (security): Reviewing + will confirm encryption sentence.

alex (sdk): I'll add the test and post link to the PR comments in a bit.

maureen (docs): Thanks everyone. If no objections, I'll merge after legal sign-off.

lee (legal): No objections from legal after quick read.

samir (security): No objections from security. :white_check_mark:

maureen (docs): Merged and backported to /v-next. Closing thread.
